# Research {.pm-title .unnumbered .unlisted}

::: pm-lede
Why do infectious diseases persist despite sustained control efforts? To what extent does perceived disease absence reflect surveillance gaps rather than genuine interruption of transmission? How can we determine where and when interventions will be most effective?

These are some of the questions that drive my research.
:::
:::

### Rabies persistence in southern Malawi

[2026 to present · Pre-PhD Research Fellowship, Worldwide Veterinary Service and Malawi-Liverpool-Wellcome Research Programme]{.pm-meta style="display:block"}

Why does canine rabies persist in southern Malawi despite repeated mass dog vaccination? This project examines spatial, temporal and programme-level determinants of persistence by integrating vaccination, animal surveillance, human exposure, post-exposure prophylaxis and contextual data.
:::

::: pm-theme
[]{.pm-ico .bi .bi-broadcast aria-hidden="true"} [Published]{.pm-status .done}

### Community-based rabies surveillance in Lilongwe

[2020 to 2022 · Lilongwe Society for the Protection and Care of Animals]{.pm-meta style="display:block"}

I designed, implemented and evaluated a community-based rabies surveillance programme in urban Lilongwe, which increased case detection five-fold, and compared it with passive surveillance to locate where cases are lost along the surveillance pathway. Related work examines how attitudes shape rabies-safe practices in the same communities.

[[BMC Public Health, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-026-30160-y)]{.pm-outputs style="display:block"}
:::

::: pm-theme
[]{.pm-ico .bi .bi-hospital aria-hidden="true"} [Published]{.pm-status .done}

### Human rabies, post-exposure prophylaxis and One Health surveillance

[2022 to 2025 · Malawi-Liverpool-Wellcome Research Programme; Pima County Health Department, Arizona]{.pm-meta style="display:block"}

In southern Malawi, I analysed health-facility, surveillance and vaccine stock data to estimate human rabies incidence, assess access to post-exposure prophylaxis, and identify gaps in data sharing between human and animal health systems. In Arizona, I assessed post-exposure prophylaxis use against risk-based guidance and developed a decision-support algorithm for wildlife exposures.

[[One Health Outlook, 2026](https://doi.org/10.1186/s42522-025-00193-1)]{.pm-outputs style="display:block"}
:::

::: pm-theme
[]{.pm-ico .bi .bi-capsule aria-hidden="true"} [Published]{.pm-status .done}

### Antimicrobial resistance and environmental infection risk

[2026 · Collaborative studies in Malawi]{.pm-meta style="display:block"}

Collaborative work on antimicrobial use and resistance in Malawi's poultry and livestock sectors, including resistance genes in *Escherichia coli* from abattoirs in Lilongwe, and a review of plastic waste as an infection hazard.

[[Antibiotics](https://doi.org/10.3390/antibiotics15030239) · [Antibiotics](https://doi.org/10.3390/antibiotics15101028) · [Frontiers in Veterinary Science](https://doi.org/10.3389/fvets.2026.1886903) · [One Health Outlook](https://doi.org/10.1186/s42522-026-00237-0)]{.pm-outputs style="display:block"}
:::

::: pm-theme
[]{.pm-ico .bi .bi-bug-fill aria-hidden="true"} [Ongoing]{.pm-status}

### Vector and wildlife ecology in Arizona

[2025 to present · University of Arizona, research volunteer]{.pm-meta style="display:block"}

Eco-epidemiological research on how urbanisation and urban greening influence West Nile virus and dengue vector ecology, including mosquito and wild bird trapping and sample collection for virus detection and genomic analysis, and a wildlife health study of pronghorn microbiome profiles.
:::
